display.purpose: Pot readout and the hand result at showdown. Slab.

money.purpose: Every currency figure. Always tabular-nums so digits never jitter.

rank.purpose: Playing card corner ranks and pips. Slab. Never on interface chrome.

label.purpose: Uppercase metric captions: POT, TO CALL, STACK, BLINDS.

shadows.name: turn-lift
shadows.purpose: The acting seat. The only persistent shadow in the system; it moves as the action moves.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: The narrow-width rail sheet raised over the table.

shadows.name: none-at-rest
shadows.purpose: Every other element, always. Depth at rest comes from tonal layering and hairlines.

motion.name: deal-stagger
motion.purpose: Delay between consecutive cards during a deal, in dealing order.

motion.name: chip-travel
motion.purpose: Chips moving from a seat to the pot on a bet.

motion.name: theme-fade
motion.purpose: Page-level palette change. Scoped to the shell only, never to gameplay state.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All deal, travel and flip motion collapses to an instant state change. Never gates the action bar becoming usable.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The turn-advancing action. Brass fill, one per region.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2px; min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 20px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: #C4952F; color: #16181A; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary small { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; opacity: 0.72; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #D9AF57; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Every non-primary control. Hairline only, no fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 44px; padding: 12px 20px; border: 1px solid rgb(22 26 24 / 20%); border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: #161A18; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: rgb(22 26 24 / 40%); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Disabled Action
components.description: An illegal action. Stays visible with its reason so a first-timer learns the rule.
components.css: .ds-btn-disabled { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2px; min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 20px; border: 1px solid rgb(22 26 24 / 6%); border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: #5A6360; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn-disabled small { font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; opacity: 0.85; }

components.name: Playing Card
components.description: The system's fixed silhouette. Theme-invariant, flat, one hairline.
components.css: .ds-card { position: relative; width: 92px; height: 128px; border: 1px solid #E3DCCB; border-radius: 6px; background: #FBF7EE; color: #16181A; } .ds-card-corner { position: absolute; display: grid; justify-items: center; font-family: Bitter, Rockwell, 'Roboto Slab', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 0.9; } .ds-card-corner--tl { top: 8px; left: 8px; } .ds-card-corner--br { right: 8px; bottom: 8px; transform: rotate(180deg); }

components.name: Seat Plate
components.description: One component for all six seats and every state. Strict slot order: name, stack, state, last action.
components.css: .ds-seat { display: grid; gap: 2px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid rgb(22 26 24 / 14%); border-radius: 10px; background: #FBF9F4; color: #161A18; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-seat-name { font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-seat-stack { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-seat-last { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #5A6360; }

components.name: Seat Plate — Acting
components.description: The turn. The only persistent shadow in the interface, paired with a brass ring so it survives grayscale.
components.css: .ds-seat-acting { display: grid; gap: 2px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid rgb(22 26 24 / 14%); border-radius: 10px; background: #FBF9F4; color: #161A18; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #C4952F, 0 4px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 18%); } .ds-seat-acting .ds-seat-name { font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-seat-acting .ds-seat-stack { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-seat-acting .ds-seat-last { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8A6420; }

components.name: Chip Stack
components.description: Denomination as encoding. Flat fill, hairline, dashed inner ring for edge spots.
components.html: $130
components.css: .ds-chips { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-chip { width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 999px; display: inline-block; position: relative; } .ds-chip::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 3px; border: 1px dashed rgb(255 255 255 / 55%); border-radius: 999px; } .ds-chip--100 { background: #202426; border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 40%); } .ds-chip--25 { background: #1E7A4D; border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 25%); } .ds-chip--5 { background: #C0392F; border: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 25%); } .ds-chips b { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #161A18; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Display name, chat, raise amount. Hairline does not move on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid rgb(22 26 24 / 20%); border-radius: 6px; background: #FBF9F4; color: #161A18; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Rail Tab
components.description: Log / Chat / Players / Manage below 1000px; the sections stack above it. Plain buttons with aria-pressed, not an ARIA tablist, because the pattern lacks roving tabindex and tabpanel roles.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; } .ds-tab { min-height: 44px; padding: 12px 16px; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; background: transparent; color: #5A6360; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab[aria-pressed='true'] { color: #161A18; border-bottom-color: #C4952F; } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Metric
components.description: POT / TO CALL / STACK readouts. Label caption over tabular money.
components.css: .ds-metric { display: grid; gap: 2px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-metric span { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #5A6360; } .ds-metric strong { font-family: Bitter, Rockwell, 'Roboto Slab', Georgia, serif; font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #161A18; }

narrative.overview: Every card room props a laminated rules card on the table. It is quiet, exact, and unglamorous, and its entire job is to tell a stranger precisely what is legal right now. That card is what this product is: a table where someone who has never played can sit down mid-game and act correctly, because the surface states the rules rather than assuming them. The world is the card-room canon played straight — broadcloth green, brass, paper cards — and it is printed flat. There is no light source in this system. The card room is delivered as a graphic system: flat inks, exact registration, hairline rules. Color follows a committed strategy: one saturated field, the felt, owns the table region outright, and everything else is neutral room, paper, or brass. The room around the table changes between themes; the felt and the cards barely move.
keyCharacteristics: Flat at rest — shadow is a state signal, never decoration
One saturated field (the felt), everything else neutral
Cards and chips are theme-invariant physical objects
Money is always tabular; digits never jitter
Density serves scanning; chrome recedes and data leads

rules.name: The Object Constancy Rule
rules.body: Cards and chips are physical objects and do not change with the theme. Card paper, card ink, suit red, and every chip denomination hold the same value in light and dark. Only the room around them flips. A card that inverts is not a card.

rules.name: The Brass Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Brass marks authority or turn and nothing else — dealer button, the acting seat, the primary action. If more than one brass element is visible per region, one of them is decoration and must be removed.

rules.name: The Chip Encoding Rule
rules.body: Chip colors mean denominations. Never reuse chip-5 red for an error, chip-25 green for success, or chip-100 black for text. State colors are separate tokens for exactly this reason.

rules.name: The Brass Contrast Ceiling
rules.body: Brass on felt reaches roughly 3.1:1 — adequate for large text, icons and UI boundaries, never for body copy. Body text on felt is paper, which clears 6:1.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every figure that can change — stack, pot, current bet, to-call, raise amount — sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. A stack that shifts width when it drops from $1,000 to $995 makes the table feel unstable during the exact moment a player is deciding.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The slab appears on card ranks and hand names. Nothing else. The moment it reaches a button or a panel heading, the distinction between object and interface collapses and the system reads as a generic themed app.

rules.name: The One Tree Rule
rules.body: No element exists twice to serve two screen sizes. A component that has a mobile- twin toggled by display: none is a defect, not an adaptation. Where wide and narrow genuinely differ, the same component moves to a different container.

rules.name: The Measured Geometry Rule
rules.body: Any layout that positions elements by computed coordinates is verified by reading back the rendered boxes at 390, 900 and 1440, not by looking at it. Zero overlaps, nothing outside its container, and no clipped money figure. A collision found by eye has already shipped once.

rules.name: The One Place Rule
rules.body: A player's identity and their position are the same drawn object. There is no roster panel listing people who are already visible on the table.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: If an element has a shadow while nothing is happening to it, delete the shadow. Gradients standing in for light are the same violation.

rules.name: The Grayscale Test
rules.body: Desaturate any screen. Whose turn it is, who has folded, who is all-in, and which actions are legal must all still be readable. This is a hard requirement from PRODUCT.md, not a preference.

rules.name: The Printed Edge Rule
rules.body: Every boundary is a 1px hairline or a flat fill. No bevels, no inner glows, no double borders, no gradient edges. If a boundary needs more emphasis, change its tone, not its dimensionality.

dos: Do set tabular-nums on every figure that can change.
Do keep illegal actions visible and disabled with a stated reason.
Do state the consequence on action buttons (Call $20 / $480 left).
Do drive responsive behavior from container queries on the table region.
Do hold cards and chips constant across themes — they are objects, not surfaces.
Do run the Grayscale Test on any screen showing player state.
Do keep the felt to 30–50% of the table view so the committed field reads as a field.
Do read back rendered geometry at 390/900/1440 before calling a coordinate-positioned layout done.
donts: Don't ship a mobile- twin of any component toggled by display: none.
Don't add a shadow or gradient to anything at rest.
Don't use brass for general emphasis — only authority and turn.
Don't borrow chip denomination colors for UI state.
Don't let the slab face escape card ranks and hand names.
Don't introduce a font size outside the six-step scale or a gap outside the 4px scale.
Don't render depth photographically — no beveled rails, no rendered chips, no felt texture images.
